patch_description: The best prior variants score ~0.80 using random + coordinate polish. The key weakness: the greedy coordinate polish moves points along axes only and the random walk spends most moves on points not in any binding triangle. I add a deterministic directed polish that (a) identifies the ~10 smallest triangles each pass, (b) for each binding vertex probes moves along the outward normal directions of the two edges adjacent to that vertex inside the small triangle (moving a vertex away from the opposite edge increases that triangle's area fastest), and (c) uses step-halving on failure. Additionally, keep 20% random kicks (via a fixed RNG) so the sweep retains exploration. This directly targets the binding constraints that define the objective, which coordinate-axis moves miss.
